outcomes: A team with no Putnami workspace creates its organization's ingest token from the CLI, signed in, and stores it as the CI upload token: putnami cloud token create --organization prints it once, and list and revoke manage it without ever printing it again
nonGoals: Creating an organization, or finding its id: the person reads it in Putnami Cloud
Tokens with another scope than delivery.ingest: identity-api gives an organization token that scope only
Workspace machine tokens: putnami cloud token create without --organization keeps creating them in the linked workspace

text: putnami cloud token create --organization <id> --name <n> [--expires <dur>] calls identity-api's POST /v1/organizations/{organization}/tokens on the control plane, under the signed-in session, with a body that holds the name and, with --expires, expires_at only.
It needs no linked workspace and runs outside any workspace; inside one, it reads only the control-plane URL of the link, when there is one.

requirements.text: putnami cloud login and logout run outside any Putnami workspace too, as putnami cloud token does, so a person with no workspace signs in before creating the organization token.

text: The text output prints the raw token once, the organization id, the warning that it is shown only once, and the paste-ready CI settings of PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN.
No other output, warning or error of the command prints the token.

requirements.text: With --organization, --scopes other than delivery.ingest, --allowed-clients or --allowed-client-ids is refused before any call, with a message that says an organization token carries delivery.ingest only.

text: putnami cloud token list --organization <id> calls GET /v1/organizations/{organization}/tokens and prints the organization's live tokens: name, scopes, creation, expiry, last use and id, never a secret.

requirements.text: putnami cloud token revoke <id|name> --organization <id> resolves the name among the organization's live tokens, refuses an ambiguous or unknown one, and calls DELETE /v1/organizations/{organization}/tokens/{id}; a token already revoked converges.
A refused call exits non-zero with the route and the server's reason; a 403 also says that the command needs platform.organization.manage on that organization.
